fields.why: Short-sleep prevalence is reported and assessed across 4 race/ethnicity groups, 4 income levels, 4 parent-education levels and 5 age groups.
Income (FPL) and parent education are SES; sex has 2 levels; special health care needs, health status and state are not SPDs.

Linear trend tests are named for income and education; race has pairwise t-tests, with 5 of 6 pairs reported (H vs Other is not), so per-group vs referent only, not all pairs. Age has no named test (it is only ranged), so side by side is right, and the flag on that entry is a false alarm: the trend test covers income and education only.

brief_issues: A methods line 'pairwise differences by race/ethnicity were determined using t-tests' implies all pairs were tested, but the brief counts 'pairwise (all pairs)' only when every pair is stated or shown; that rule decides it here.
